input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: perf: quick-pick-survey information selector pair loop (largest landable consumer after owner-gated P063/P064)

errors.what: First full simulation run used npm ci --ignore-scripts, so pooling.simulation.test.ts could not load the Prisma client (suite exit 1 in both phases)
errors.fix: npx prisma generate, then ran that file alone on both versions: 13/13 pass each

errors.what: The first parity test missed changes to the repeat penalty (0.5, 0.04)
errors.fix: Added a fixed case that brackets the penalty between 0.0493 and 0.0512; every behaviour-changing mutation fails now

doc_friction.issue: Both open perf backlog items (P063, P064) touch CODEOWNERS paths again; the prompt already says to skip to steps 2-4, which worked.

The stop hook asks for a commit while a long before/after benchmark has the original file swapped into the working tree; I staged the new blob with git update-index instead. A note on benchmarking from a separate worktree would avoid this.

deviations.why: Its top suggestion was worker threads for cell(); a profile showed the time was in the pair loop itself, which also serves the live route
deviations.did: Optimised the loop in place, keeping the floats exact
deviations.result: Suite 630 s to 151 s, MEASURE output byte-identical, and live selector 3-5x faster at 500 items

notes: Metric: quick-pick-survey simulation suite wall time (npx vitest run --config vitest.simulations.config.ts --reporter=json, 4-core container, back to back): before 630 s, after 151 s (poolCapDeep4000 555 to 150 s, pairMix 238 to 70 s, poolCapDeep2000 129 to 38 s). The 14 MEASURE lines are byte-identical; 41/41 tests pass both times (plus pooling 13/13 both after prisma generate). Live selector (pairLatency.test.ts with PAIR_BENCH, median of 15 calls): at 500 items and 300 answers, information 32.9 to 12.8 ms, staged 49.5 to 10.0 ms. Profile (node --cpu-prof, cell(500,800,1), 9.1 s to 2.0 s): pairKey array, sort and join per pair, plus per-pair closures, were most of the self time. npm run verify exit 0 (470/470 tests, build ok). Parity test: 10 behaviour-changing mutations all caught. CI check-run result in PR.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: profile, exact-float rewrite of a hot loop, parity test with mutations, two 10-minute benchmark runs, docs and post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
